slides.headline: 6 AI PROMPTS THAT TURN 1-STAR REVIEWS INTO REPEAT CUSTOMERS
slides.image_prompt: A single colossal five-pointed gold star — skyscraper-tall — looms over a tiny brick storefront at night, its amber glow flooding the building like a threat. No readable signage. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh flash, film grain. Accent: blazing amber against deep navy sky.

slides.headline: 1) TURN A 1-STAR REVIEW INTO A RESPONSE THAT WINS THEM BACK
slides.body: A restaurant owner tried this; the customer came back and updated to 4 stars. Use this: "Write a response under 100 words that acknowledges the specific complaint and offers one concrete next step."

slides.headline: 2) FIND THE PATTERN QUIETLY KILLING YOUR REPUTATION
slides.body: A gym owner pasted 40 negative reviews into Claude and found 3 hidden problems he'd missed for months. Use this: "List complaints appearing more than once, rank by frequency, give one fix each."

slides.headline: 3) CATCH UNHAPPY CUSTOMERS BEFORE THEY POST PUBLICLY
slides.body: After one business added a follow-up text, unhappy customers started reaching out privately instead of going public. Use this: "Write two texts, Version A for reviews, Version B for complaints, each under 60 words."

slides.headline: 4) WRITE A RESPONSE TO A COMPLAINT GOING VIRAL
slides.body: Most businesses post something they regret. Claude writes a better response in 30 seconds. Use this: "Write a public reply under 120 words, take responsibility, state one specific change, no corporate language."

slides.headline: 5) GIVE YOUR WHOLE TEAM A WORD-FOR-WORD SCRIPT
slides.body: A salon owner spent 6 months training staff on complaints. Claude produced the full script in 4 minutes. Use this: "Five-step phone script: vent, validate, apologize, fix, confirm. Each step under 20 seconds."

slides.headline: 6) TURN A FIXED COMPLAINT INTO A LIFELONG CUSTOMER
slides.body: Most owners stop at the fix. Use this: "Write a 3-email sequence: today, then 2 weeks with a surprise offer, then 60 days asking for a review. Each under 100 words."

slides.headline: SAVE THIS
slides.body: You'll want these the next time a bad review lands. Save this post. Daily AI news and real skills.

caption:
Swipe through these 6 prompts. 🔖 Each one handles a real moment most business owners dread, and each takes 30 seconds to use.

1) turn a 1-star review into a response that wins the customer back, 2) find the pattern in your negative reviews, 3) catch unhappy customers before they post publicly, 4) write a public response when a complaint goes viral, 5) give your team a word-for-word script for angry customers, 6) turn a fixed complaint into a lifelong customer

Most business owners ignore bad reviews or spend an hour writing something they regret. These prompts handle it in 30 seconds. They work for any business where a customer can leave a public rating.

Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this could do for yours.

Sources: Anthropic

editor_override: Cover image fails the thumb test (§3). The giant glowing gold star over a brick building is symbolic decoration — at feed size, a cold scroller reads 'star rating' at best, never 'AI prompts' or 'fixing a bad review.' Image Law requires PROOF or a STAGED SCENE of the story. Fix: replace with a human face — a business owner staring at their phone with a visible 1-star notification, or a split-scree
